evidence.note: Installs boto3 and runs a series of ~10 python heredoc scripts against the running service, indicating real boto3 client verification of core operations rather than assuming correctness.
Iterative fix→recompile→restart→retest loop, including checking audit.log output, showing verification is used to catch and correct defects, not just a one-off.

Further restart and python test with data cleanup; no visible console DOM/testid checks, no concurrency load test, and no browser-side UX verification — the harder half of the grader's loop is absent.

reasoning: The agent clearly runs the real boto3 client against core operations in a fix-and-retest loop, exceeding ad-hoc curl (level 3), which places it at the level-5 anchor: real boto3 round-trips plus some error/edge checks. However there is no evidence of a repeatable harness spanning header+query signing, the full edge-behavior set, a concurrency/corruption test, or any console DOM/testid verification, so it falls short of the level-8 anchor. The abbreviated log (no observation content) limits confidence in exactly how deep the boto3 scripts probed.
